newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy says Europe needs NATO, Russia deal.
newsitem.headline: Italy says Europe needs NATO, Russia deal.

text.p: The Italian foreign ministry said on Saturday that Russian President Boris Yeltsin's decision to sign a charter building a new relationship between Moscow and NATO was good news for Europe.
"This represents a fundamental element for the construction of a more stable framework for security and peace within Europe," a spokesman at the foreign ministry said.

Yeltsin agreed at the two-day summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton in Helsinki to press ahead with a new NATO charter despite Moscow's continued opposition to the eastward expansion of the alliance.

Italy also welcomed news that Russia would be an active participant in the next Group of Seven (G7) most industrialised nations summit in Denver, Colorado in June, saying this had been an Italian "objective". Italy is a member of the G7.

The foreign office spokesman said Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov would visit Italy in the coming weeks for talks with his Italian counterpart, Lamberto Dini. The exact date of the trip still has to be fixed.
